coverageNote.note: We audited the 18 active US aluminum beverage-can and can-end plants Ball operates. Ball's wider footprint (international plants, the Boulder aerospace business, and the divested aluminum-cup JV) sits outside the beverage-can yard network and is excluded by design.

account.dossierIntro: Ball runs its aluminum can plants around the clock, and empty cans leave by the trailer-load, so every plant is outbound-dominated. The yard is the throttle on how fast finished cans reach the filling lines. We audited the 18 active US beverage-can and can-end plants Ball operates: 476 dock doors and 857 trailer positions across 677 acres, almost all of it moving by truck, with only 3 sites touching rail. The tell is at the gate. Eleven of the eighteen plants run as open truck yards with no gate control and no guard booth at all, including Pittston PA, the single largest yard we mapped at roughly 60 docks and room for 150 trailers. YardFlow puts one orchestrated gate-to-dock move over every one of them.
surprisingFindings: Eleven of the eighteen plants run as open truck yards with no gate and no guard booth, so nothing controls when trailers arrive or leave.
Pittston PA is the biggest yard we mapped: 88 acres, about 60 dock doors, room for 150 trailers, and no gate control at all.
Findlay OH is the outbound hub, a guarded 95-acre campus with about 70 docks and 150 trailer spots, and the only site with a staffed guard booth.

sites.name: Ball - Golden CO

Manufacturing). Four can-manufacturing lines; produces 8/12/16/24-oz bodies plus ends
and a CapCan line; ~95M cans/day; ~360 employees. Corroborated by the Golden Chamber
member listing at 4525 Indiana St and a 2024 Ball-hosted Women in Manufacturing factory
tour of the plant. Ran the closure gauntlet: this site is NOT among Ball's 2022-2024
North American plant closures (Phoenix, St. Paul MN, Wallkill NY, Kent WA, Verona VA
slug plant). Company-operated, owned. `verdict = confirmed`.

fieldNotes.truckGate: No controlled truck gate at the operational interface. The south dock apron ('EAST DOCKS' signage, 2025-08 Street View) is open to the public road with tractors and trailers backed directly into dock doors, no barrier arm, no guard booth, no manned checkpoint. Perimeter is partial chain-link with sliding yard gates (west drive, 2022 SV) but the primary truck/dock access is uncontrolled.
fieldNotes.guardShack: None observed walking the frontage road east, west, SE and SW panos (2019-2025).
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimate. Long dock line along the south face of the main block ('EAST DOCKS'); ~5-6 trailers visible backed in at capture, banks extend across the south wall. 25-50 band is a modeled estimate for a plant of this output (4 can lines, ~95M cans/day).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Freight-trailer rows staged NW of the plant between the building and the rail corridor (~25-40 trailers). Note: a separate RV/boat storage lot sits further NW at the reservoir edge and is excluded.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spur runs along the north edge of the property into the plant (visible track, NW-SE corridor).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Golden/Arvada industrial corridor within the Denver metro fabric.
